youtube.baslik: Why does the eardrum move more easily when the ossicular chain breaks? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: When the ossicular chain breaks, the tympanic membrane is freed from the load of the cochlea and moves much more easily than normal; the tympanogram peak can rise markedly, giving a type Ad curve. A type Ad curve is always read together with the audiogram, because a thin eardrum can produce the same curve with normal hearing.
